Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the term sheet — looks promising. A few immediate questions from our side before we take this to legal/finance:

1) Invoicing entity: we prefer an EU invoice where possible to simplify VAT handling. Do you have an EU entity that can invoice us?
2) Currency / FX: Can you invoice in EUR? If invoices come from a US entity in USD that creates FX volatility for our P&L.
3) Withholding tax: Our local counsel asked whether any payments to Redwood will be subject to domestic withholding tax and what documentation you can provide to reduce/avoid WHT (tax residency certificate, VAT ID, etc.).

Also — is the 20% up-front prepay refundable if we overestimate consumption, or is it fully earned? We need clarity on true-up mechanics.

Thanks — Marco

Subject: RE: FW: FinServe questions on invoicing entity / WHT / FX — need quick guidance

Soojin — summary from Finance with recommendations:

Options for invoicing and tax handling:

1) Invoice from Redwood Europe Ltd (preferred for client)
   - Pros: EU VAT handling straightforward; we can issue invoices with VAT where applicable or net invoices with reverse-charge note if customer is VAT-registered in their country. Avoids USD->EUR FX for the customer.
   - Cons: We'd need to ensure entity has current VAT registration in the customer's jurisdiction (we do for NL/IE/UK depending on country). Slight delay for tax admin (we can do within 3 business days once entity chosen).

2) Invoice from Redwood Inc. (US) in USD or EUR (FX exposure handled via conversion)
   - Pros: Faster (no inter-entity billing).
   - Cons: Creates FX noise for the customer. If invoiced in USD, they may ask for gross-up on any withholding tax. We can offer an FX pass-through or fixed exchange rate for the invoice if they prepay.

Withholding tax (WHT):
- Typically payments for SaaS services aren’t subject to WHT in most EU jurisdictions if treated as services, but that depends on local rules. To mitigate: upon request we can provide a Certificate of Tax Residency (US/EU entity) and commercial invoices with appropriate references. If FinServe's local counsel asserts WHT applies, we will work with them on language to apply treaty benefits; that may require a tax residency certificate and signed declarations from the customer.

Refund/true-up:
- Our standard prepay is non-refundable but we offer quarterly true-up with credits for unused committed usage (credit applied to future invoices within 12 months). For large enterprise deals we can consider a partial refund clause under specific conditions — would need Legal sign-off and likely reduce the overall discount.

Suggested path: propose Redwood Europe Ltd invoice in EUR; provide certificate of tax residency for Europe entity and include reverse-charge language if applicable. Offer carryforward credits for unused prepay and a 12-month window. If they insist on US invoicing, offer fixed FX rate for the first 90 days and provide residency docs for WHT discussions.

I'll prepare a short finance note (1-pager) with the residency and VAT steps we need.

Laura Bennett
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

To: Marco Rossi <m.rossi@finserve-global.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@finserve-global.com>

Subject: Re: Proposed multi-year prepay term sheet for FinServe Global

Hi Marco — thanks for the questions and patience. Following our internal review, proposed approach below (we've also attached an updated term sheet and SOW):

- Invoicing entity: Redwood Europe Ltd will invoice FinServe in EUR. We will issue VAT-qualified invoices and include reverse-charge notation where applicable. (If you confirm country of registered entity, we will set the correct VAT ID on the invoice.)
- Currency / FX: Invoices will be in EUR. For any charge billed in USD during migration windows, we will apply a fixed EUR/USD rate for 30 days to limit FX volatility.
- Withholding tax: We will provide a Certificate of Tax Residency for Redwood Europe Ltd to support treaty benefits where relevant. If your local counsel still requests gross-up or WHT, we'll negotiate case-by-case and include standard WHT indemnity language.
- Refunds / true-up: Prepay remains non-refundable. We offer quarterly true-up with credits for unused consumption, credit valid for 12 months. For this enterprise transaction we can discuss a partial refundable tranche if required — will affect discounting.
- Ramp schedule / discount: Proposed 3-year ramp: 40% of committed usage in year 1 (discounted at 18%), 30% year 2 (15%), 30% year 3 (12%). Annual renewal credits for overage.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm the invoice recipient (billing contact + VAT ID and country).
2) If you need the Certificate of Tax Residency from Redwood Europe Ltd, confirm and we will attach within 48 hours.
3) I'll loop in Legal for WHT clause if requested.

Attachment: Redwood_FinServe_MultiYear_TermSheet_v3.pdf; FinServe_SOW_Q3.xlsx

Would you like to hop on a 20-minute call Monday to finalize?

Best,
Soojin

Hi Soojin — this approach works for us. A couple of final housekeeping items before finance processes the PO:

- Billing contact and VAT: please route invoice to FinServe Global B.V. (EU entity). Billing email: finance@finserve-global.com. Our VAT ID (NL): NL123456789B01.
- Certificate of Tax Residency: please send the residency certificate for Redwood Europe Ltd so we can apply treaty benefits and avoid any WHT.
- PO and payment terms: we'll issue a PO for the 3-year prepay; can we keep net30 on the invoice?

We appreciate the flexibility on EUR invoices and the fixed FX window. Once we have the certificate and the updated term sheet you can expect the PO within 5 business days.

Marco
